rationales: Solid particles dispersed in gas are not mist.
Gas dispersed in liquid is not mist.
Mist consists of tiny liquid droplets dispersed in gas.
Gas dispersed in a solid is not mist.
CH₄ is nonpolar and is not appreciably soluble in water.
NaCl dissolves in water to form hydrated ions.
C₂H₄ is largely nonpolar and poorly soluble in water.
C₆H₆ is nonpolar and poorly soluble in water.
Benzene does not produce ions in solution, so it is a non-electrolyte.
HCl ionizes in water and conducts electricity.
NaOH dissociates into ions in water and conducts electricity.
CH₃COOH partially ionizes in water, so it is a weak electrolyte.
Protons are charged and are less penetrating than neutrons.
Electrons are charged and are less penetrating than neutrons.
Neutrons have high penetrating power because they carry no charge.
Alpha particles are relatively weakly penetrating and are stopped easily.
C₆H₁₂O₆ is the molecular formula, not the simplest whole-number ratio.
CH is not the simplest ratio of the atoms in glucose.
Dividing the glucose formula subscripts by six gives the empirical formula CH₂O.
C₆H₆ is not the formula of glucose.
Eight grams of CO₂ is about 0.18 mol, not 0.15 mol.
The amount is 8 ÷ 44 ≈ 0.18 mol.
Eight grams of CO₂ is not 0.21 mol.
Eight grams of CO₂ is not 0.24 mol.
The long-form periodic table is arranged by increasing atomic number, not Mendeleev’s postulate.
The long-form periodic table is based on increasing atomic number.
Atomic mass is not the basis of the modern long-form periodic table.
Mass number is not the basis of the long-form periodic table.
Hydrogen has the lowest molar mass among these gases and diffuses fastest.
Helium is heavier than hydrogen, so it diffuses more slowly.
Fluorine molecules are much heavier than hydrogen molecules and diffuse more slowly.
Chlorine molecules are much heavier than hydrogen molecules and diffuse more slowly.
NH₃ has a complete octet around its nitrogen atom.
BF₃ is electron deficient because boron has only six electrons around it.
Each nitrogen atom in N₂ attains an octet through the triple bond.
Each oxygen atom in O₂ attains an octet in the molecule.
A covalent bond pair contains more than one electron.
A covalent bond pair consists of two shared electrons.
Three electrons do not make a bond pair.
Four electrons are not a bond pair.
Chalk does not dissolve and its particles can settle, so chalk in water is a suspension.
Chalk particles in water are not a stable colloidal dispersion.
Chalk does not dissolve uniformly to form a true solution.
Chalk is the dispersed solid, not the name for the mixture; the mixture is a suspension.
Sulphur is generally not lustrous.
Phosphorus is generally not lustrous.
Iodine is a lustrous non-metal.
Carbon is not generally lustrous, though some forms such as graphite can appear shiny.
Isotopes are atoms of the same element with different mass numbers, not different forms of an element.
Allotropes are different forms of the same element in the same physical state.
Amorphous describes a non-crystalline solid structure, not different forms of an element.
Crystalline describes an ordered solid structure, not different forms of an element.
A concentrated solution of common salt in water is called brine.
Benzene is a separate chemical compound, not salt water.
Alcohol is not the name for concentrated salt water.
Toluene is a separate chemical compound, not salt water.
Opal is not a liquid dispersed in a gas.
Opal is not a solid dispersed in a gas.
Opal is commonly treated as a solid-in-solid solution of silica containing water.
Gas dispersed in a solid is not the usual classification of opal.
